identity.title: ALMA Resolves C I Emission from the β Pictoris Debris Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We resolve C I emission at 492 GHz using ALMA and study its spatial distribution.

evidence.quote: around a 1.75 M$_\Sun$ star (cite: Crifo_etal_1997), seen edge-on

question.value: What is the spatial distribution and mass of atomic carbon (C I) in the beta Pic debris disk, and does C share the CO clump asymmetry?

evidence.quote: We resolve C I emission at 492 GHz using ALMA and study its spatial distribution. C I shows the same clump as seen for CO.
project ID 2013.1.00459.S, PI: Brandeker
We observed the $\beta$ Pic disk using band 8 receivers of ALMA on December 19, 2015

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 3 SPWs of 1920 channels, 488 kHz spacing (937.5 MHz) on C I, CS 10-9, SiO 11-10; 4th SPW 128 channels, 1875 MHz at 479 GHz for continuum

evidence.quote: three spectral windows, each with 1920 channels and a channel spacing of 488 kHz (total bandwidth 937.5 MHz)
CS 10–9 at 489.75 GHz
SiO 11–10 at 477.50 GHz
The array consisted of 36 antennas arranged in a hybrid configuration

baselines.value: 15 m to 6.3 km; baselines >2 km flagged

evidence.quote: We therefore flagged all baselines longer than 2 km, effectively removing one third of the baselines.
The beam size is 1.18$''$$\times$0.95$''$ (23 au$\times$19 au)
($\sim$70 mJy beam$^{-1}$) in the individual channels

time_on_source.value: 2.1 h total, 1.2 h on beta Pic; median pwv 0.6 mm

evidence.quote: The total integration time was 2.1 h (with 1.2 h on $\beta$ Pic)
on December 19, 2015 during the ALMA cycle 3 Early Science campaign
project ID 2013.1.00459.S, PI: Brandeker

provided.value: C II fluxes and spectrally resolved line used with C I

evidence.quote: previously published spectrally resolved *Herschel*/HIFI observation of C II
Luca Matrà kindly provided the ALMA CO 3–2 and 2–1 data as well as the model of the dust radiation field.
previously published spectrally resolved *Herschel*/HIFI observation of C II (cite: Cataldi_etal_2014)

what.value: C II PACS flux from summed spaxels

evidence.quote: we sum the flux values of the PACS spaxels listed in their table 1

pipeline_or_manual.value: Manual standard calibration with WVR and Tsys; bad antennas DA44, DA54 flagged

evidence.quote: We performed standard water vapour radiometre (WVR) calibration and system temperature corrections.
The data were calibrated using CASA 4.7.0 (cite: McMullin_etal_2007).

flux_calibrator.value: J0522-3627 used for bandpass and flux

evidence.quote: we discarded the data from the two flux calibrators and instead used J0522-3627 to calibrate both bandpass and flux
We then imaged the visibilities using the `CLEAN` task within CASA.
we applied a taper of 1$''$
we performed continuum subtraction using the `uvcontsub` task within CASA
We did not correct for the primary beam, as it changes the total flux only within the quoted error bars

final_beam.value: 1.18'' x 0.95'' PA 44 deg (line); 1.19'' x 0.96'' PA 46 deg (continuum)

evidence.quote: The beam size is 1.19$''$$\times$0.96$''$ (23 au$\times$19 au) with the position angle of the major axis being 46$^\circ$.

what.value: Deprojection of pv diagram following earlier work (edge-on, flux in front of sky plane)

evidence.quote: for simplicity, we follow (cite: Dent_etal_2014) and assume that the disk is edge-on
For the mean molecular weigh $\mu$, we follow (cite: Matra_etal_2017) and assume $\mu=14$.
We fix $\phi_{\mathrm{c}}=-32\ensuremath{^\circ}$ (cite: Matra_etal_2017).

what.value: Chi2 definition analogous to Booth et al. eq. 2

evidence.quote: we assign a $\chi^2$ measure by using expressions analogous to equation 2 in (cite: Booth_etal_2017)

unstated_but_needed: CLEAN parameters (weighting/robust, cell, image size, threshold, masks, channel width of cubes)
Pixel positions of rectangular boxes and p-v region mask definition
Dust radiation field model from Kral+2017 (private communication) and CO cubes

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image C I cube and continuum

method.value: CASA calibration, flag baselines >2 km, uvcontsub, tapered CLEAN

evidence.quote: We then imaged the visibilities using the `CLEAN` task within CASA.
we applied a taper of 1$''$

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line flux, profiles and pv diagram

method.value: Moment 0 within +-6 km/s, rectangular aperture photometry, errors from emission-free sample volumes; pv restricted region

evidence.quote: integrating the data cube along the spectral axis within $\pm6$ km s$^{-1}$

validation.value: Compared with single-dish flux of Higuchi et al.

evidence.quote: The measured flux is consistent with the value of $(1.7\pm0.4)\times10^{-19}$ W m$^{-2}$

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate total carbon mass with 1D non-LTE model

method.value: pythonradex (RADEX-like) uniform sphere, electrons as colliders, fit C II (PACS) and C I flux over Tkin 40-1000 K

evidence.quote: we use `pythonradex`, a python implementation of the RADEX code

key_parameters.value: b = 0.57 km/s; sphere volume equals torus with 35 au x 10 au

evidence.quote: Here we used $b = 0.57$ km s$^{-1}$, derived in appendix

assumptions.value: Carbon ionisation provides the electrons; uniform sphere geometry

evidence.quote: photoionisation of carbon is the main electron source
increasing or decreasing the radius of the emitting sphere by 50% does not change the lower bound by more than 15%

analysis_steps.goal: 3D models of ring, ring+clump and eccentric gas

method.value: Grid search with chi2 summed over C I (ALMA) and C II (HIFI); T=75 K isothermal; ionisation balance and SE solved per cell

evidence.quote: We sum the $\chi^2$ from the *Herschel*/HIFI data (C II) and the ALMA data (C I).
we consider isothermal models and fix $T_\mathrm{kin}=75$ K everywhere

fitting.value: grid search chi2, parameter ranges in Tables 1-2

evidence.quote: Explored parameter space and best fit values for the ‘ring’ and ‘ring + clump’ models

validation.value: LIME full radiative transfer differs by at most factor 1.2

evidence.quote: the total flux computed by `LIME` differs at most by a factor 1.2 for both C I and C II

method.value: Gaussian fit to vertical cut at x=0 of pv diagrams, emcee MCMC

evidence.quote: We use 100 walkers with $10^4$ steps.

fitting.value: emcee, chi2 likelihood, uninformative priors with positivity

evidence.quote: We consider invariant, uninformative priors, imposing only that the peak of the Gaussian and the broadening parameter are positive.

validation.value: Three independent measurements combined by weighted mean

evidence.quote: Combining these measurements as a weighted mean yields $b=0.57\pm0.03$ km s$^{-1}$.

method.value: C mass divided by CO mass loss rate using revised CO lifetime of 50 a

evidence.quote: a CO lifetime of 50 a leads to a CO mass loss rate of $1.2\times10^{11}$ kg s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Constant CO loss rate; C only from CO; no C removed

evidence.quote: 1) the CO mass loss rate is constant, 2) C is produced only from CO photodissociation
The data were calibrated using CASA 4.7.0

used_for.value: non-LTE radiative transfer for 1D model and 3D models

evidence.quote: we use `pythonradex`
We estimate errors using `emcee`
we used the `LIME` code version 1.9.1
we determine a total carbon mass between $5\times10^{-4}$ and $3.1\times10^{-3}$ M$_\ensuremath{\oplus}$
we find a timescale between $1.7\times10^3$ and $1.1\times10^4$ years
The SW/NE flux ratio (within the same box as in figure 1) is now $1.2\pm0.2$.

findings_qualitative.value: No C I emission beyond ~120 au or inside ~50 au; no atomic accretion disk

evidence.quote: no atomic accretion disk has formed (yet) as there seems to be little C I emission inside of $\sim$50 au

claims.hypothesis: Does C I share the CO clump asymmetry?
claims.experiment: Resolved C I map and profile compared with CO
claims.result: C I follows CO 2-1 profile with SW peak
claims.finding: Asymmetry is real, though statistical significance is marginal

evidence.quote: Thus, the significance of the peak ratio asymmetry is only marginal.

claims.experiment: C mass divided by CO loss rate

evidence.quote: indicating that gas production started only recently (within $\sim$5 000 years)
the accretion profile predicted by (cite: Kral_etal_2016) produces too much C I emission in the inner regions of the disk

claims.result: C integrated over ~10 orbits should be spread

evidence.quote: For $\beta$ Pic, our resolved C I observation excludes this possibility.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Giant impact, resonance trapping, secular forcing disfavoured

evidence.quote: our observation disfavours a few proposed scenarios (planet MMR trapping, giant impact, secular forcing)

limitations_admitted.value: Data did not initially pass QA2 due to low elevation and array configuration

evidence.quote: the data initially did not pass Quality Assurance 2 (QA2)

limitations_admitted.value: Uniform sphere geometry is a clear limitation; masses are first-order

evidence.quote: The assumption of a uniform sphere is thus a clear limitation of this model.

referee_caveats_inferred: No error bars on dynamical mass or grid-search parameters
Mass upper bound sensitive to temperature, volume and b
